constraints: Door authorization reads badge active/revoked state.
Audit export is allowed to lag after revocation succeeds.

details.mechanismOrProperty: One badge state is the consistency unit for this command; an export can consume its later update without joining that unit.
details.scenarioApplication: For this badge, the immediate door decision reads access state; it does not wait for the delayed audit export.
details.errorCorrection: If door authorization still reads an active value after success, the stated revocation result is false even if an audit row exists.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The premise separates an immediate access rule from a lag-tolerant report, so expanding the boundary to all doors or reports is unnecessary.
details.transfer: Use the same rule when a command has one immediate decision and a separate projection with an explicit lag budget.

messages.text: A door could still grant access after the command reports success, which violates the stated authorization boundary.
The door configurations and lag-tolerant audit do not participate in the one-badge revocation invariant; site-wide scope adds unrelated contention.
The export is explicitly allowed to lag, so it cannot be the authority for an immediate access decision.
The facts require a coherent badge access decision, not a lock over independent readers and a lag-tolerant export.

feedback.reason: The command may report success only after authorization no longer sees the badge as active, while audit export has an explicit lag allowance. Keep the access state together and let the audit projection follow.

options.text: Commit revocation to the audit log first and let each door cache learn about it on its next refresh.
Put every badge, door configuration, and audit export for the site into one aggregate.
Commit the badge’s revocation and access state in one boundary.
Let the audit export decide whether the badge is revoked when a door asks for authorization.
Require a distributed lock across every door and audit consumer before revocation can succeed.

prompt: At a smart-building site, the facilities team revokes a badge after an employee leaves. The door policy must never grant access from a badge record that still says active after the revocation command reports success. A separate audit export may lag by a minute. Which consistency boundary fits?

constraints: The label request identifies one approved shipment revision.
Printing status may be retried without changing that revision.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The request should carry an immutable revision identity so the worker can render the approved address even if a later revision exists.
details.scenarioApplication: The print worker follows the revision named by the operator’s approval, even if another address revision is later created.
details.errorCorrection: Reading current mutable fields or assembling rows in the screen can silently substitute a different address for the one named by the request.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Only the revision-to-label meaning is coupled here; printer attempts do not become part of the shipment invariant.
details.transfer: When asynchronous work must represent a chosen revision, persist that reference instead of expanding the aggregate to include worker mechanics.

messages.text: A later edit could make the label differ from the revision the request approved.
Printer retries do not change the approved shipment revision, so grouping them with shipment data couples independent work.
A retry is for the same named revision; making a new shipment for each attempt changes shipment identity.
That leaves the revision association to a caller and can mix fields from different approved versions.

feedback.reason: The approved revision is the value the label request promises to represent, but a printer retry changes only delivery status. Preserve that reference and keep retry bookkeeping separate.

options.text: Have the printer read whichever address is currently on the shipment when its worker runs.
Put the shipment, printer queue, and every retry counter in one aggregate.
Create a new shipment aggregate for every print attempt.
Let the operator screen assemble label fields from separate address and shipment tables.
Bind each label request to its approved shipment revision.

prompt: After an address correction, a shipping operator approves a shipment revision and requests a package label. Each label must show the address from the approved revision named by that request. Printing status can be retried independently. What should share the consistency boundary?

constraints: Overlapping bookings for one room cannot exceed 20 attendees.
Cancellation fees do not affect occupancy and are calculated later.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The room-level boundary can compare the incoming attendees with its current overlapping reservations before accepting the move.
details.scenarioApplication: A move consumes capacity in the destination room only for bookings whose times overlap the moved rehearsal.
details.errorCorrection: Checking only the booking misses concurrent occupants; a tenant-wide lock includes rooms whose reservations cannot affect this capacity rule.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The scenario requires a valid confirmed schedule, not eventual repair after an over-capacity commitment.
details.transfer: Choose the smallest consistency boundary that can evaluate all values participating in the invariant.

messages.text: A single booking can fit while the combined overlapping bookings exceed room capacity.
The invariant is per room and overlapping time; unrelated rooms do not contribute to the capacity count.
The fee is explicitly independent of occupancy and runs later; it cannot arbitrate whether the destination room has space.
That leaves a confirmed schedule violating the immediate capacity invariant.

feedback.reason: The destination decision depends on the combined overlapping bookings for that room, not only the moved booking. The later fee calculation has no role in whether the room can accept it.

options.text: Check only that the moved booking has at most 20 attendees, then accept it.
Arbitrate the room’s overlapping reservations at its capacity boundary.
Lock all rehearsal bookings for every room in the tenant before any move.
Recalculate and commit the cancellation fee before changing room occupancy.
Accept the move and repair over-capacity schedules during the nightly report.

prompt: A rehearsal scheduler moves a booking between rooms. Each room has a fixed capacity of 20; two overlapping bookings may not exceed it. A customer cancellation fee is calculated later and does not affect room occupancy. Which boundary should arbitrate the move?

constraints: The maintenance mode used by command validation.
Temperature readings are read-only and do not enable movement.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The state boundary needs the mode used to accept or reject a movement, while telemetry can be recorded without changing command eligibility.
details.scenarioApplication: The arm command is accepted or rejected using the exhibit’s current maintenance mode; a temperature observation is not that mode.
details.errorCorrection: A disabled screen button cannot protect a controller that accepts commands from other callers; checking temperature substitutes the wrong fact.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The scope is one exhibit’s command rule, not a transaction over all exhibits or telemetry storage.
details.transfer: Keep the state that governs an immediate command decision with that decision; separate observations that do not participate in it.

messages.text: Temperature is explicitly not the signal that permits or rejects arm movement.
The guard applies to one exhibit arm; unrelated exhibits and read-only readings do not join that invariant.
That applies the guard after the unsafe action instead of rejecting the command while maintenance is active.
The premise is a controller command rule; a UI-only check does not govern other command callers.

feedback.reason: The controller must evaluate the maintenance state at the same decision point as the movement command. Temperature telemetry is not part of that guard and can remain an independent feed.

options.text: Infer maintenance mode from the most recent temperature reading before each movement command.
Group every exhibit and all incoming telemetry in one state boundary.
Move the arm and then record that maintenance was active.
Keep maintenance mode and the arm-command guard in the exhibit state.
Let the technician’s screen disable the movement button and trust that no other caller can send the command.

prompt: An exhibit controller enters maintenance mode before a technician opens a panel. While maintenance is active, commands that move the display arm must be rejected. Read-only temperature telemetry may continue arriving independently. Which state belongs together for command validation?

constraints: Retirement stops new assignments but preserves the lesson identity for existing progress.
The retirement report is a nightly rebuild.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The lesson lifecycle state can close future assignment while leaving the stable lesson identity and existing progress intact.
details.scenarioApplication: Learner progress continues to reference the same lesson while the catalog stops offering it to new assignments.
details.errorCorrection: Rewriting progress or changing its ID would contradict the explicit continuation rule; waiting for a report leaves assignment eligibility stale.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This operation changes one catalog lifecycle fact. It does not require a bulk edit of learners or synchronous report regeneration.
details.transfer: Keep lifecycle state with the entity whose future use it governs; preserve historical references when the scenario requires them.

messages.text: Existing learners may continue and progress refers to the stable lesson ID, so deletion breaks the stated relationship.
Progress is allowed to continue under the same identity, and the report is rebuilt later; neither needs to be rewritten for retirement.
A nightly report is not the stated authority for allowing new course assignments.
That changes the stable identity that existing progress is required to keep.

feedback.reason: Retirement changes whether new assignments may select the lesson, not which lesson existing progress refers to. The nightly report is a downstream projection and does not belong in that state change.

options.text: Retire assignment availability while keeping the lesson’s stable ID.
Delete the lesson row and rewrite each learner’s progress to a replacement lesson.
Include every learner progress record and nightly report in the lesson retirement transaction.
Wait for the next report rebuild to decide whether new assignments can use the lesson.
Create a new lesson ID for retirement and redirect old progress to it.

prompt: A learning library retires a lesson from new course assignments. Learners who already started it may continue, and their progress uses the lesson’s stable ID. The retirement report is rebuilt nightly. Which change should be atomic with retirement?

constraints: The close marker separates the exported event sequence.
Email notification may be delayed.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The session decision identifies the last included event; the worker can use that fixed boundary even when notification is delayed.
details.scenarioApplication: The persisted close marker defines the event cutoff that the delayed export worker must use.
details.errorCorrection: Current events at worker time are not equivalent to events committed before close, and process-local markers cannot define a durable export boundary.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Only one session’s ordered history participates in this decision; the email provider is a separate effect.
details.transfer: For a delayed consumer, store the domain boundary it must honor instead of relying on the caller’s memory or timing.

messages.text: Email delivery does not define the session’s committed event boundary.
That ignores the explicit close marker and can change the export after the session was closed.
The boundary is one session’s event sequence; unrelated boards do not contribute to it.
A delayed worker needs the committed boundary, not a marker that disappears with the host process.

feedback.reason: The export is defined by the session sequence around its persisted close marker; email timing is independent. Persist the marker and sequence boundary before asking a worker to export.

options.text: Wait for the email provider to accept a notification before deciding which events belong in the export.
Export the latest events whenever the worker runs, including events committed after close.
Commit the close marker with the session event-sequence boundary.
Lock every board session while one session closes and exports.
Keep the close marker only in the host process and let the export worker infer it later.

prompt: A whiteboard session host closes a board for export. The export must contain all events committed before the close marker and none committed afterward. An email notification may be delayed. Which values must be decided together at close?

constraints: Owner and response deadline form one accepted escalation result.
The activity feed may update afterward.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Treat the paired values as one conversation transition and let the feed consume the accepted result.
details.scenarioApplication: The conversation is observed as escalated only when its owner and response deadline reflect the same transition.
details.errorCorrection: A separate write can expose a mismatched pair, and a lagging feed cannot safely reconstruct the authoritative state.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The scenario couples two fields on one conversation, not every conversation sharing a queue.
details.transfer: When the caller observes a paired state change as one result, keep those values within the same consistency decision.

messages.text: The conversation could temporarily show the new owner with the old deadline even though the prompt requires one accepted result.
The feed may lag, so it cannot be the authority for the accepted conversation state.
The paired owner/deadline change concerns one conversation; the whole queue does not participate in that transition.
That exposes a partially accepted transition to other callers, contrary to the stated same-result requirement.

feedback.reason: The command has one visible result: a new owner paired with its response deadline. A lagging activity feed can record that transition afterward without serving as its authority.

options.text: Change the owner now and recompute the deadline in a later job.
Let the activity feed reconstruct the current owner and deadline for each caller.
Group every conversation in the specialist queue into one aggregate before any escalation.
Have the escalation screen issue separate owner and deadline writes and retry whichever fails.
Commit owner and deadline as one conversation transition.

prompt: An escalation desk raises a conversation to a specialist queue. The assigned owner and response deadline must change in the same accepted escalation; a separate activity feed may update afterward. Which boundary should own acceptance?

constraints: Price and stock must pass both checks before the listing becomes searchable.
Search indexing may lag after publication.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The listing transition owns the joint price/stock check; search can catch up without reopening that validity decision.
details.scenarioApplication: The listing becomes searchable only after its own price and stock values satisfy the publication checks.
details.errorCorrection: An eventually updated index cannot enforce a pre-publication condition, and checking only price omits one required value.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The consistency scope is one listing; no fact requires a transaction across every seller listing or the index.
details.transfer: Separate a state transition’s required facts from a read projection that may be refreshed afterward.

messages.text: The index is allowed to lag and is not the authority that prevents an invalid listing from becoming published.
The prompt requires both values before publication, so a valid price alone is insufficient.
Only one listing’s two checks participate in this decision; seller-wide and index state are separate.
The stated publication rule requires nonnegative stock, not a stale projected value.

feedback.reason: Publication depends on two current listing facts, while indexing is explicitly allowed to lag. Validate both before changing the listing’s published state and project the result later.

options.text: Publish first and let the search index reject listings with invalid price or stock.
Validate current price and stock in the listing publication transition.
Check positive price but defer stock validation until the first purchase.
Place every listing, seller account, and search index document in one aggregate.
Treat the latest stock projection as sufficient even if the listing’s current stock is negative.

prompt: A marketplace publishes a seasonal listing. A listing is searchable only when its price is positive and available stock is nonnegative; the search index can lag after publication. Which boundary should decide publication?

constraints: Each child shipment retains the request ID and delivery promise.
Vendor confirmations may arrive independently and reporting combines them later.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The request transition records children linked to the parent; each vendor response updates its own confirmation state.
details.scenarioApplication: Each vendor child remains attached to the same parent request even though vendor acknowledgements arrive at different times.
details.errorCorrection: Creating unrelated child request IDs breaks the stated association, while requiring all vendors to confirm invents cross-vendor atomicity.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The request identity is shared across the split; the external confirmations remain independently arriving facts.
details.transfer: When a business decision must preserve a parent relationship but collaborators respond independently, avoid grouping their entire lifecycles together.

messages.text: The vendors confirm independently, so waiting for all of them changes the stated workflow and creates a cross-vendor transaction.
That loses the original request identity the scenario explicitly requires every child to retain.
The view is built later from independent confirmations and is not the authority for the parent request identity.
Independent vendor confirmations and a later report do not need to change the identity-preserving split decision.

feedback.reason: The split plan must preserve one parent request identity and promise, but independent vendor confirmations do not form one synchronous outcome. Keep the plan decision local and let the report combine later confirmations.

options.text: Require every vendor to confirm before any split plan can be recorded.
Give each vendor child a new request identity and copy the delivery promise into it.
Let the combined reporting view own the split plan and decide whether the request exists.
Commit the split plan under the parent request’s identity and promise.
Put vendor confirmation states and reporting rows inside one request aggregate.

prompt: A fulfillment specialist splits a backordered request across vendors. The child shipments keep the original request ID and promised delivery date; each vendor can confirm independently. A reporting view combines confirmations later. What should remain one domain transition?

constraints: The plot has at most one active reservation throughout an accepted transfer.
Approval history is append-only and may be exported later.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The plot-scoped reservation decision must arbitrate the old-to-new assignment together.
details.scenarioApplication: The plot’s active reservation changes from the former gardener to the new one without exposing an empty or duplicate slot.
details.errorCorrection: Changing one record without checking the slot can create a duplicate; two independent commits can expose the forbidden empty interval.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Only the reservation slot for this plot is coupled; the append-only export can lag.
details.transfer: When uniqueness is defined across several records, put the arbitration at the smallest boundary that can see those records.

messages.text: The field update alone does not prevent two active reservations for the same plot.
The invariant is scoped to the transferred plot; other plots cannot create a second active reservation for it.
The history export is later and does not decide whether the plot has exactly one active assignment.
That exposes a state with no active reservation despite the accepted transfer’s stated continuity rule.

feedback.reason: The transfer’s correctness is defined at the plot slot: accepted state must have one active gardener rather than a duplicate or gap. Exporting approval history does not participate in that invariant.

options.text: Transfer the plot’s active-reservation slot in one coordinated change.
Change only the reservation’s gardener field without checking the plot’s active slot.
Lock every plot in the garden while transferring one reservation.
Wait for the approval-history export to finish before updating the active reservation.
End the old reservation, commit, and create the new one in a later independent request.

prompt: A garden steward transfers a reservation from one gardener to another. The plot has one active reservation; the transfer must leave either the old gardener or the new gardener assigned, never both and never neither. Approval history is append-only and may be exported later. What state must be coordinated for transfer?

constraints: An issued quote references exact component revisions and its adjustment.
Later component prices do not alter an issued quote.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Treat the quote as the immutable record of those exact inputs, while current product pricing evolves independently.
details.scenarioApplication: The issued quote remains tied to the component revisions and adjustment selected when that quote was made.
details.errorCorrection: Reading live prices or looking up the adjustment later would replace values that the prompt says are fixed on the issued quote.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This boundary preserves one quote’s historical inputs; it does not require all catalog prices to share its lifecycle.
details.transfer: Keep a priced decision’s exact inputs with that decision when later source values are allowed to change.

messages.text: That would change an issued quote after the fact, contrary to the fixed revision and adjustment facts.
An issued quote is fixed by its referenced revisions; unrelated products do not contribute to that quote.
The quote itself includes a fixed adjustment, so a later lookup could substitute another value.
The region supplies a value used in the quote; the prompt does not require distinct bundle behavior or all historical prices.

feedback.reason: The quote’s promised amount is tied to both its referenced component revisions and the fixed adjustment. Later catalog changes must not recalculate that already-issued result.

options.text: Recalculate every issued quote from the latest component prices whenever it is read.
Include every regional product price in one aggregate so no quote can become stale.
Commit component revisions and the adjustment in an immutable quote.
Store component revisions now and look up the regional adjustment only when checkout occurs.
Create a different bundle type for each region and embed all component price history in it.

prompt: A packaging service creates a regional bundle from component products. At quote time, the bundle stores the exact component revisions and a fixed regional adjustment; later component price changes must not rewrite an issued quote. Which values must the quote preserve together?

constraints: The charger has no overlapping active reservations.
Expired holds are excluded before accepting a new reservation.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The charger-scoped schedule can evaluate the complete interval set needed for non-overlap.
details.scenarioApplication: A reservation is checked against every active interval on that charger after expired holds are excluded.
details.errorCorrection: Checking one reservation misses competing intervals, and waiting for nightly cleanup contradicts the explicit expiry rule.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The rule is scoped to one charger and its active holds, not every charger or a separate maintenance index.
details.transfer: An invariant over a set requires the decision boundary to see the relevant set, but not unrelated data.

messages.text: A different active reservation may occupy the same interval, so a single-record check misses the invariant.
The index describes maintenance notes, not the active reservation intervals named by the rule.
The non-overlap rule is per charger; unrelated intervals on other chargers do not affect this slot.
The prompt says an expired hold frees its interval before a new reservation is accepted.

feedback.reason: The request must be compared with all active intervals for its charger after expired holds are excluded. Maintenance notes have no bearing on slot availability.

options.text: Check only whether the requested interval overlaps the reservation being edited.
Use the maintenance-note search index to decide whether the time slot is free.
Lock every charger in the network for each reservation request.
Count expired holds as active until a nightly cleanup job removes them.
Arbitrate the charger’s current reservation intervals together.

prompt: A charging coordinator reserves time on one charger. Reservations must not overlap, and an expired hold frees its interval before a new reservation is accepted. Charger maintenance notes are read-only and may be indexed later. Which boundary should arbitrate a reservation?

constraints: The survivor asset ID stays stable and receives the selected descriptive values.
The retired-ID redirect may be rebuilt later.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Keep the survivor identity and selected values together in the merge; rebuild the redirect from the committed result.
details.scenarioApplication: The chosen metadata is written to the stable survivor; a rebuildable redirect can be refreshed from that outcome.
details.errorCorrection: Creating a new identity or picking the last stored duplicate contradicts the explicit stable-ID and selection facts.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The redirect can lag without changing the merged domain asset, so it is not part of the acceptance decision.
details.transfer: Separate a domain object’s committed values from a derived lookup structure when the latter is explicitly rebuildable.

messages.text: The prompt says the survivor ID remains stable; a new identity would change references for a descriptive correction.
The redirect is explicitly rebuildable later and does not define the survivor’s metadata values.
Only the survivor’s selected values change; unrelated photographs do not participate in this merge.
Storage recency is not the stated selection rule for title and rights values.

feedback.reason: The merge changes descriptive fields on the chosen stable survivor, while the old-ID redirect is a rebuildable projection. Storage recency does not choose the winning metadata.

options.text: Create a new asset identity for each metadata correction and point the survivor to the newest one.
Apply the selected metadata to the stable survivor asset.
Require the redirect projection to update before accepting the metadata merge.
Include every photograph and every redirect in one merge transaction.
Replace the survivor with whichever duplicate record was most recently stored.

prompt: An archive curator merges duplicate metadata for a photograph. The survivor asset ID remains stable; the chosen title and rights statement replace the old values, while the redirect from the retired ID can be rebuilt later. Which state belongs in the merge result?

constraints: A work-territory pair has at most one active approval.
Other territories are independent; audit display may lag.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The pair-scoped boundary can reject a second active approval without serializing unrelated territory decisions.
details.scenarioApplication: Only approvals for the same work and territory compete for the one active slot.
details.errorCorrection: Global uniqueness disallows stated independent approvals; expiry alone does not enforce one active record for the same pair.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The display is a projection, and only the specified pair belongs in the consistency scope.
details.transfer: Derive boundary size from the exact uniqueness key rather than widening it to the whole catalog.

messages.text: The prompt permits independent approvals for other territories, so global uniqueness is broader than the stated rule.
The display may lag, so it cannot reliably arbitrate current active approval state.
Expiry bounds each approval but does not remove the explicit one-active-approval uniqueness requirement.
Only the same work-territory pair participates in uniqueness; unrelated pairs do not need a shared decision.

feedback.reason: Uniqueness is scoped to one work-territory pair, while other territories are explicitly independent and the audit view may lag. The acceptance decision needs only the pair’s active approval state.

options.text: Allow only one active approval for the work across all territories.
Let the audit screen decide whether a new approval is a duplicate.
Accept any number of active approvals and use expiry to choose one at read time.
Arbitrate active approvals within one work-territory pair.
Put all works and territory rules in a single global approval transaction.

prompt: A rights analyst approves a work for a named territory until a fixed expiry. There may be at most one active approval for the same work and territory; approvals for other territories are independent. The audit screen can lag. Which scope should own approval acceptance?

constraints: A battery has at most one current aircraft assignment.
Maintenance plans are independent; history may be written afterward.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The battery-scoped assignment decision prevents two active links while leaving aircraft maintenance planning independent.
details.scenarioApplication: The old and new aircraft links are evaluated by the same battery identity during reassignment.
details.errorCorrection: Checking only the destination model misses a duplicate for this battery; writing both links before reconciliation violates the one-current-assignment fact.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The rule is per battery, not a transaction over the fleet or its maintenance schedules.
details.transfer: Locate a uniqueness invariant by its actual key and coordinate updates for that key.

messages.text: The stated uniqueness is per battery, so a model-level check does not prevent the same battery being assigned twice.
History may be delayed and is not the authority for the battery’s single current assignment.
The uniqueness applies to one battery; unrelated maintenance plans do not join the assignment invariant.
That creates an interval where the same battery has two current assignments, which the prompt forbids.

feedback.reason: The unique key is the battery’s current assignment, so reassignment must arbitrate the old and new aircraft against that same battery state. History can follow as a record of the result.

options.text: Arbitrate reassignment through the battery’s current-assignment boundary.
Check only that the destination aircraft has no battery of this model.
Append a history row and let each aircraft screen decide which assignment is current.
Put every battery, aircraft, and maintenance plan in one aggregate.
Create the destination assignment before removing the prior one and reconcile duplicates later.

prompt: A fleet coordinator assigns a battery to an aircraft. A battery may have only one current aircraft assignment, but aircraft maintenance plans are managed independently. Assignment history can be written after the current assignment changes. Which state should arbitrate reassignment?

constraints: Consent must be current for the referral-recipient pair when send is authorized.
External delivery may fail after local acceptance.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The authorization record is scoped to the referral-recipient pair, and delivery status records the later external outcome.
details.scenarioApplication: The local referral-recipient authorization is decided before the separate delivery attempt begins.
details.errorCorrection: A copied flag can be stale, and successful transport cannot establish that consent was valid before the attempt.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The scenario distinguishes a local decision from an external effect; it does not promise atomic delivery.
details.transfer: Keep an authorization fact with its decision while representing remote effects through their own outcome lifecycle.

messages.text: External delivery can fail after local acceptance, so the facts do not promise one atomic operation across both systems.
The rule says consent is current, and the prompt gives no freshness period for a stale copied flag.
The decision is for one referral-recipient pair; unrelated patients and recipients do not participate.
Delivery success says nothing about the separate authorization fact that must be checked before sending.

feedback.reason: The local system decides whether this referral may be sent to this recipient using current consent; the external attempt can fail later. Do not claim that the network call joins the local transaction.

options.text: Include the external clinic’s delivery system in the same atomic transaction as consent evaluation.
Authorize from a long-lived copied consent flag on the referral.
Commit current-consent authorization for the referral-recipient pair.
Lock all referrals and consent records for the clinic during one send.
Treat a successful network delivery as proof that consent was current.

prompt: A clinic navigator sends a referral only when consent is current for that referral and recipient. The consent ledger records grants and withdrawals; delivery attempts are external and can fail after acceptance. What should the local decision boundary cover?

constraints: Completion links to the exact exercise and scoring-policy revisions.
Profile changes are independent; history projection is asynchronous.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The completion stores the two revision references as part of its own recorded outcome.
details.scenarioApplication: The completion record retains both revision references even when profile or reporting data later changes.
details.errorCorrection: Resolving current policy or relying on a lagging projection can change or omit the historical basis of the score.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The prompt couples the completion to its inputs, not to the mutable learner profile or its reporting projection.
details.transfer: Persist the references that define a completed decision with that outcome; keep mutable presentation state separate.

messages.text: That can display a different policy from the one used to score the completed exercise.
Neither profile changes nor the later projection changes the recorded inputs for this completion.
The prompt requires exact revision references, not a profile copy that can later change.
An asynchronous projection may lag or be rebuilt; it is not the authoritative completion record.

feedback.reason: The completed result is meaningful only with the exact exercise and scoring-policy revisions used. Profile edits and the asynchronous history view do not alter those inputs.

options.text: Store only the exercise ID and resolve the current scoring policy when history is read.
Include the learner profile and asynchronous history projection in the completion commit.
Copy the current policy fields into a mutable learner profile and use that as the historical record.
Let the history projection be the only place where completion revision references are stored.
Commit the completion with its exercise and scoring-policy revisions.

prompt: A practice tracker records a learner’s completed exercise. The completion must retain the exact exercise and scoring-policy revisions used; the learner’s current profile can change independently. A history projection is rebuilt asynchronously. Which state should the completion commit?

constraints: Reviewer identity and both passed controls are required in the approval record.
The pending-exception index may lag.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The exception decision stores its required reviewer and control evidence, while the pending index follows the committed result.
details.scenarioApplication: This exception is approved with its reviewer and both control results; the search index can then catch up.
details.errorCorrection: A bare flag loses the facts that justify approval, and a lagging index cannot stand in for the control results.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The consistency boundary is one exception’s decision, not the entire procurement queue.
details.transfer: When a record’s accepted status depends on evidence, keep the decision and that evidence together; let search projections lag.

messages.text: The index may lag and therefore cannot be the authority for the approval decision.
That exposes an approved record without the required control results.
Only this exception’s reviewer and control results define the acceptance; unrelated cases do not.
The approval record must identify the reviewer and control results; a UI check and bare flag do not preserve those facts.

feedback.reason: Approval is defined by the reviewer and the two control outcomes on this exception; the lagging index is only a search projection. Accept those decision facts together before updating the index.

options.text: Let the pending index decide whether both controls have passed before recording approval.
Commit the exception approval with reviewer and control results.
Record the reviewer first and attach control results later.
Place every exception and every reviewer assignment in one aggregate.
Have the reviewer screen hide the approve button until controls pass, then store only an approved flag.

prompt: A procurement exception is approved only after two named controls pass. The approval record must identify the reviewer and control results together; a search index of pending exceptions can lag. Which boundary should accept the decision?
